blocks.text: Setting up your SEO workspace on Mac

Since Google Sheets runs in the browser, your Mac experience depends on how you manage your tabs. Do not let your browser window become a graveyard of dead links. Install Google Sheets as a Progressive Web App. Open your sheet in Chrome, click the three dot menu, go to Save and Share, then select Install page as app. This gives you a dedicated icon in your dock. It keeps your SEO data separate from your casual browsing.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for SEO speed

SEO work involves a lot of cleaning and formatting. You need to be fast. Press ⌘ + / to open the full list of shortcuts. Use ⌘ + ⇧ + H to find and replace bad characters in your keyword lists. When you have a massive crawl export, use ⌘ + ⌥ + 9 to hide rows you do not need right now. It keeps your view clear.

You likely work with files containing thousands of rows. When you import a CSV from Ahrefs or Semrush, the data often comes in messy. Use Data > Split text to columns to break apart comma separated values. If you see duplicates, use Data > Data cleanup > Remove duplicates. Always keep a raw copy of your data in a separate tab before you start editing.
Building client reports in Google Sheets

Clients want to see trends, not just raw numbers. Use pivot tables to summarize your organic traffic data. Select your range, go to Insert > Pivot table. Drag your date field to Rows and your sessions to Values. This makes it easy to see month over month growth. Keep your report tabs clean by hiding gridlines in View > Show > Gridlines.

Do not hardcode your formulas. Use cell references instead. If you copy a formula down a column, make sure your ranges are locked with dollar signs like $A$1. This prevents errors when you sort your data. Also, avoid using too many complex array formulas in one sheet. They slow down your browser and make the sheet lag during client meetings.
How to get help while working

When you are deep in a technical audit and get stuck on a VLOOKUP or a filter, do not stop your flow. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where to find a specific feature. Lazur will point at the menu item or guide you through the steps. It saves you from searching through help articles while you are in the middle of a task.

Importing data from Screaming Frog is a daily task. Go to File > Import > Upload to bring in your crawl data. If the numbers look like text, select the column and use Format > Number > Number to fix the formatting. This is vital for running correct calculations on your site speed or word count metrics.

faq.question: Is there a native Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google Sheets is a web application. You can create a desktop shortcut using Chrome to make it act like a native app.

faq.question: How do I handle huge SEO datasets in Sheets?
faq.answer: Sheets supports up to 20 million cells. If your file is slow, try moving older data to an archive sheet or using pivot tables to summarize large ranges.

faq.question: What is the best way to share reports with clients?
faq.answer: Use the Share button to give view-only access. This prevents clients from accidentally changing your formulas or deleting your data.
